title: intento, silent h, ahora, voy, v as soft b

cards.title: intento = I try / I'm trying
cards.body: The -o ending shows 'I', just as in quiero. Intento relates to 'intention' and means 'I try' or 'I'm trying'. There's no -ation rule here, but recognising the family helps you understand it.

examples.en: I'm trying to imitate it / him.

cards.caveat: One Spanish present-tense form covers both 'I try' and 'I am trying'.

cards.title: h is silent
cards.body: Spanish h is never pronounced. Don't even think it: imagine hospital starts with o.
cards.caveat: Except in ch, which sounds like English 'ch'.

cards.title: ahora = now
cards.body: Ahora (h silent) is a + hora, 'to the hour'. That gives you two more words: a (to, towards) and hora (hour).

cards.title: Build long sentences piece by piece
cards.body: A long sentence is just blocks: quiero / cancelarlo / pero / no quiero / cancelarlo / ahora.

examples.en: I want to cancel it, but I don't want to cancel it now.
examples.es: Quiero cancelarlo, pero no quiero cancelarlo ahora.

cards.title: voy = I go / I'm going
cards.body: Link voy to 'voyage'. Spanish v usually sounds like a soft b (vamos, 'let's go', sounds like 'bamos'); in some areas, such as around Argentina and Chile, you'll hear more of a v. Either is understood.

cards.title: visitar
cards.body: 'Visitation' exists in English (as in visitation rights), so the -ation rule gives visitar.

cards.title: Soft b and a real s
cards.body: Keep the s as s, not English z. The soft b has no puff of air, unlike English b in 'bucket'; a paper in front of your mouth shouldn't move. Using a v is fine too.

practice.why: Same word; the h is silent.

practice.en: I want to cancel it, but not now.
